comment: Prompt templates for card art (issue #49), after the style guide's prompt structure (docs/design/bird-collection/style-guide.md, 'Art direction'): the place's palette, the bird's anatomy and markings kept, subtle light, no typography, borders or logos. Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 reads them as instructions about its input images. Fields: {common_name}, {scientific_name}, {place}, {edition_light}, {edition_colors}, {edition_motifs}, {light}. Pack art uses the edition's motifs; scene and photo art only its light and colours, because a motif would be a claim about a place the photo does not show. Version 2 (the bake-off's second to fourth rounds, DECISIONS.md): scene and photo art no longer name the species, because a name pulls in the model's idea of the species (a red finch became a Northern Cardinal, a female or young bird a bright male), and the Legendary light keeps the bird's true colours. Version 3: scene art paints edge to edge, because version 2 sometimes ended in a ragged white paper edge. Version 4 (the maintainer's wording, 2026-10-14): an epic fantasy adventure-cover look in richly layered opaque gouache, with the bird kept entirely natural, after version 3 painted too tamely. Version 5: scene art paints a composite (packbuilder.art.paste_bird pastes the reference bird into the zoomed glasses photo), so its template keeps the pasted bird where it is instead of adding one from image 2; and a negative prompt, which counts now that the workflows run at full quality (cfg 4). Version 6: scene art takes the photo-art wording (keep the photographed moment), because at full quality the 'wilderness encounter' wording replaced a sharp glasses scene with an invented fantasy valley while this one kept it. The editions' themes live here until the packs' set definitions carry them (#54, #57). Bump the version when a template, an edition or a light changes.

light.standard: Add subtle atmospheric light and a few quiet gold flecks.
light.legendary: Light it dramatically with a warm golden rim light around the bird, a luminous sky, deep soft shadows and drifting gold motes; the bird keeps its true colours.

negative: a photograph, photorealistic rendering, a photo with a texture filter, blurry, low resolution, text, letters, watermark, logo, border, frame, paper edge, a second bird, extra birds, deformed anatomy, extra legs, extra wings, armour, clothing, jewellery, glowing eyes

templates.pack:
Transform image 1 into an epic fantasy adventure-cover painting of a {common_name} ({scientific_name}) from {place}. The bird is the central character in a grand wilderness quest: a real creature presented with the presence and dignity of a legendary encounter.

Paint in richly layered, opaque gouache with sculpted brush strokes, bold masses of light and shadow, selective fine feather detail, and a tactile, hand-painted surface. Use the visual language of classic tabletop fantasy campaign art: luminous focal light, deep atmospheric shadows, rich pigments, and an ancient, mysterious world. The image must unmistakably read as a painting.

Preserve the bird from image 1: its anatomy, proportions, pose, silhouette, plumage colours, and diagnostic field marks. Preserve its sex and age characteristics. A dull female or juvenile remains dull; lighting must not invent brighter plumage or new markings. Keep the eye, bill, and wing tips unobstructed.

Build a new, immersive background using {edition_motifs}. Arrange these elements as dramatic environmental framing, giving the scene depth and a sense of discovery while keeping the bird dominant. Apply {edition_colors} primarily to the environment and atmospheric shadows. Illuminate the scene with {edition_light}. {light}

Create wonder through composition, paint, atmosphere, and light. The bird remains entirely natural: no armour, clothing, jewellery, magical anatomy, or invented plumage.

Paint edge to edge. No typography, letters, borders, frames, logos, or watermarks.
templates.scene:
Repaint image 1, a photograph with a real bird pasted into it, as an epic fantasy adventure-cover painting, using the existing photographed moment as the complete composition.

Use richly layered, opaque gouache with a matte painted surface, visible directional brush strokes, sculpted forms, and bold, deliberate light-and-shadow shapes. Simplify incidental background detail into expressive painted masses while retaining precise detail around the bird's eye, bill, and identifying markings. The result must clearly look hand-painted, not like a photograph with a texture filter.

Preserve the bird exactly as it appears: its pose, anatomy, proportions, silhouette, and field marks. Preserve the local plumage colour of every body region, including the head, throat, breast, back, and wings. A dull female or juvenile must remain dull. Do not invent iridescence, brighten feathers, or replace the bird with an idealised breeding male.

Preserve the photograph's framing, viewpoint, setting, and object placement. Keep the bird where it is and at its size; blend it into the scene with believable contact, perspective, and shadows, adding only what it needs to stand on, such as a twig, branch, or stone. Do not add scenery, landscape, props, creatures, or accessories.

Bring the drama of a classic fantasy quest illustration entirely through painterly execution and lighting: luminous highlights, deep but readable shadows, and a strong focal hierarchy around the bird. Embellish the existing light with {edition_light}, and let {edition_colors} shape the environment and atmosphere without recolouring the bird. {light} Keep the bird's diagnostic colours readable beneath the lighting.

No armour, clothing, magical anatomy, glowing eyes, or invented plumage. Paint edge to edge. No people, typography, letters, borders, frames, logos, or watermarks.
